statement:
Point $P$ lies on the circle with equation $(x-2)^2+(y-1)^2=16$.

Point $Q$ lies on the circle with equation $(x-4)^2+(y+5)^2=16$.

What is the maximum possible length of $PQ$?
solution:
The two circles have centres $C_1=(2,1)$ and $C_2=(4,-5)$, both with radius $4$.

The distance between the centres is
$$C_1C_2=\sqrt{(4-2)^2+(-5-1)^2}=\sqrt{4+36}=\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{10}.$$

The farthest two points on the two circles are obtained when $P$ and $Q$ lie on the line through the centres, on opposite (outer) sides. The maximum distance is then the centre distance plus both radii:
$$PQ_{\max}=C_1C_2+4+4=2\sqrt{10}+8,$$
which is **option F**.
hints: Find the centres and radii of the two circles.
The maximum distance uses the distance between centres plus both radii.
Compute the centre distance with the distance formula.
